summary: Encode accepts any complete set of frame files, so a partial or low-quality re-render into the default frame directory is later published as the canonical video.
failure_scenario: After a full canonical render, run `render_motion.py --frames 10 --spp 1` (default --out is build/frames/dolly, allowed because fps/count are canonical), or stop a full re-render with build/STOP_GPU midway, then run `render_motion.py --encode --no-render`. All 216 files exist, so encode writes build/out/dolly.mp4 from a mix of old, new and 1 spp frames with no error.
evidence: Source trace, not executed. render() (lines 340-398) only overwrites the scheduled files and never clears the directory; check_frame_directory allows the canonical directory for canonical settings; encode() lines 164-167 checks only is_file() per index and then writes to OUT because canonical is true. --encode with --frames is rejected, but the two-step form is not.

summary: Recorded poses are written as matrix4d time samples, which USD interpolates element-wise, so any evaluation between samples yields a non-rigid (shrunken, sheared) transform.
failure_scenario: A recorded body that rotates tens of degrees per sample (for example a spinning part recorded at --fps 30, or 10 rev/s at 120 Hz) is viewed at a fractional replay time: the observer playhead is continuous (30 Hz render against 120 Hz samples, 0.001 s slider steps) and snapshot capture uses f/fps. The body shrinks between samples and returns to full size on sample times.
evidence: Stdlib probe executed on the math only: linear blend of two Y rotations at the midpoint gives column length 0.99966 at 3 deg per sample, 0.9945 at 12, 0.9659 at 30, 0.8660 at 60 (determinant 0.999, 0.989, 0.933, 0.75). USD interpolating matrix4d linearly is from knowledge of the library, not run here because pxr is not installed. Separate translate and orient ops (quaternion slerp) avoid it. Slow bodies such as the four-bar probe are barely affected.

summary: Frames are encoded as limited-range BT.601 with no colorimetry tags, but players treat untagged HD H.264 as BT.709, so colors shift.
failure_scenario: A 1280x720 Dolly or Orbit360 MP4 is played in a browser or common player that assumes BT.709 for HD. Round trip of RGB (255,0,0) decodes as about (255,25,0) and (60,180,90) as about (51,163,88).
evidence: Arithmetic probe only, using the exact coefficients in the kernel and the BT.709 inverse. Player behavior for untagged streams is from knowledge and was not run. tools/check_loop.py compares against NVDEC output from the same untagged stream, so it cannot detect a matrix mismatch. Docs record the range choice but not the matrix.

summary: Errors from polling and commands are never cleared by later success, so a transient or already-resolved error stays shown.
failure_scenario: The observer lists revisions/*.usdz, then the publisher finishes pack and replaces current.json, then the observer reads current.json: revision N is not in the stale listing, so the error 'Publication not available: the current revision is not published' is set. The next poll resolves it, but state['error'] is cleared only when a candidate revision is accepted (line ~306) or the pending message clears. With the user pinned to an older revision (follow False) no candidate starts and the false error stays on screen. A rejected 'seek' (line 189) likewise persists until a revision switch.
evidence: Source trace of observe(): state['error'] is assigned at lines 152, 189, 210 and 258 and reset only in the candidate-success branch and the pending-message branch. Race ordering follows the glob at line 136 versus the read at line 143. Not executed.

summary: Reported translation and rotation are measured against the first recorded sample, which is taken after the first physics step, not against the authored initial pose.
failure_scenario: A body that moves during step 1 (a strong drive, initial velocity, or joint or overlap correction) has that motion excluded; a body that jumps once in step 1 and then stays still reports zero travel in feedback.json, which the constructor reads as no motion.
evidence: Source trace: simulate.py records seconds = arange(1, steps+1)/fps with the sample appended after step_sync, so poses[0] is the post-step-1 pose; measure() subtracts positions[0] and quaternions[0]. No pre-step pose is stored. Not executed.

summary: The loop check decodes with NVDEC and nvImageCodec in a process that never builds a GpuPacer, so it gets no priority, affinity or stop handling.
failure_scenario: Running check_loop.py on the desktop starts GPU decode at normal priority with full CPU affinity and ignores build/STOP_GPU, contrary to the rule that shared GPU workers go through tools/gpu_work.py. Work is small (eight frames), so impact is limited.
evidence: grep shows gpu_work is not imported by check_loop.py or by image_io.read_rgb, which it calls at line 10 and elsewhere.

summary: gpu_work: affinity mask selection (lowest four allowed CPUs, half of system CPUs on small systems), idempotence of a repeated mask, BELOW_NORMAL class value 0x4000, D3DKMT IDLE value 0, stop checks before and after each batch and during idle waits, and rest computation all match CLAUDE.md and tools/check_gpu_work.py by source reading.

rtx.converge and render_motion: ordinals, seconds-based update_from_usd_time, warmup order, loop guards, device mapping release and per-batch pacing around the readback are consistent. Native runtime separation holds: only sample_transforms, viewer_scene, physics_usd, engine and publish import pxr, each in its own process, and rtx.py, simulate.py and observe.py do not.

sample_transforms: a default-valued override in the strongest layer wins over weaker time samples at any numeric time, time is seconds times the source timeCodesPerSecond, and non-transform or instance-proxy animation is rejected as documented. A render override layer composes below the sampled poses.

video_pixels NV12 layout (full Y plane then interleaved Cb,Cr, 2x2 chroma average at even coordinates), the BT.601 limited-range coefficients, video_io packet timing at 90 kHz with B-frames off, IDR de-duplication, partial-file cleanup, and image_compute tent weights (sum 2*f^2, edge clamp, exact integer rounding) were checked by reading and small arithmetic.

publish/pack: packages are built under a temporary non-numeric name and replaced into place, and current.json is replaced atomically, so the observer never lists a partial numeric revision. viewer_scene camera framing, the Swizzle BGRA product and the app.js event names and signaling port agree with observe.py. probe_mechanism joint frames, hinge anchors and four-bar closure are geometrically consistent.
